('One turn from an unset chord mask', {'expected': ('2nd', '-7th'), 'shown': ('X', '-6th')})

rationale: The four channel-wide chord mask handlers seeded an unset chord mask as -1, but for chords 0 is X and -1 is '-7th' (the refresher and display treat unset as 0). One turn up from unset therefore stayed on X and one turn down skipped -7th to -6th (baseline screen: ('X', '-6th')). The seed is now 0, so the first turn moves one chord step from X. Behaviour-helper cascade: cases that set channel chord masks counted turns from the old -1 seed; their turn counts drop by one (strum_reset_continuity, arp_basic_timing, spread_acceleration_contract, fractional_spread_contract, minimum_swung_gap_contract, muted_sparse_reverse_arp, arp_rest_live_scale, chord_shape_schedule, panic_pending_chord in cases.py; numeric_length_merge strum, mask_full_chord_inheritance, mask_clear_combined_chords and the mask_clear_attributes chord default), and the two explicit-Off chord slots (arp_rest_slots, arp_empty_muted_replacement), which were one turn from -1, are now one turn up and back. Expected notes are unchanged. The channel_edit_mask_handler characterisation units for unheld increment/decrement from unset now pin +1/-1 for the chord handlers.
oracle: Human decision 2026-09-11 (S26): an unset chord mask should start from X. README 597 (a channel mask adds a chord note to every trigger) for the audible check; the chord labels are characterisation.
